start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:read-glance-feeds with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"} and surface watch with limit 20."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the feed reads the person's own rows of the record types the definitions name, in whatever form the store keeps them.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:read-glance-feeds" with store, and either a feed id or a surface, and a limit if you want fewer than 50 rows per feed.
3. The first run reads the definitions and proves the read on the example rows; every attempt must come out as the prove step says, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run answers each feed from the store's own rows in the order the definitions give.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The store keeps habit rows h1 (Doing, entry path present, Walk), h2 (Stopped), h3 (no entry path) and h4 (Doing, entry path present, Read).

worked_examples.title: A watch surface, limited
worked_examples.ask: Show the watch surface with 1 row per feed.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The watch surface lists habits, pursuits, told, ai-work, running and decisions in that order.
worked_examples.hands_back: feeds in the order "habits", "pursuits", "told", "ai-work", "running", "decisions", each with at most 1 row.
